title: Critical Minimax Modulus for Two Dose Cohorts under an Affine Calibration Benchmark
banked_reason: Stage 0.5.G: paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, so graded field is capped at subfield; not salvageable within scope.
gap_reasons: The sharp minimax conclusions are proved only for conditional-affine procedures under homoskedastic Gaussian errors and an exact global affine cohort drift; minimaxity over unrestricted measurable procedures remains open in unrestricted-frontier.

The bounded-nonaffine extension establishes a Gaussian affine sensitivity frontier but no corresponding random-design value transfer, so its practical guarantees are strictly weaker than those of the affine benchmark.
The continuum certificate is proved to terminate uniformly, yet the note supplies neither a certified numerical curve nor reproducible implementation artifacts
paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4, so the graded tier 'field' is capped at 'subfield'.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the conditional-affine Gaussian frontier, uniform rational continuum certification, random-design transfer for exact affine drift, and a full-line independent-control sensitivity extension with a critical-radius certificate; mathematical review passed without findings. The field-tier claim fell below the novelty floor because unrestricted minimaxity and nonaffine random-design transfer remain open, and no certified numerical curve or implementation artifact was delivered. A new field-level attempt needs a re-anchored result rather than another in-scope D0 repair.
tldr: Two random-design Gaussian dose cohorts observe a common twice differentiable response on overlapping dose ranges under a conditional affine calibration benchmark for the second cohort. At \(w_n=\kappa n^{-1/5}\), an exact four-term reflection calculation reduces the affine-drift quotient to the bounded-acceleration half-line value \(I_\kappa=4J_{\kappa/2}\). Free-terminal finite-horizon dual relaxations, compactly stopped primal paths, and rational density give all-real compact-range certificates with zero uniform gap. Under pinned non-affine drift, reflection is unavailable: the corrected sensitivity certificate remains on the full line, with independent response and drift curvature controls coupled only through the quadratic observation loss. Its uniformly convergent decision envelopes support critical-drift-radius reports with certified strict bounds or an honest ordinate-tolerance band at equality and flat contact. The Gaussian affine frontier and sharp moving-support random-design value equalities remain the estimation-and-inference headline; no random-design sensitivity transfer or unrestricted nonlinear minimaxity is claimed.
gap: Donoho's and Armstrong--Kolesár's formulas are inherited decision theory for an already known attained modulus; they do not solve the two-channel affine-drift quotient. Existing random-design equivalence theorems do not deliver sharp values under moving support. Cohort-specific slope models motivate an affine calibration benchmark but neither imply it nor quantify bounded non-affine failure.
fill: The paper gives a finite rational-cell primal--dual program with explicit seam and tail penalties, proves compact-range continuity and zero uniform gap, establishes the quotient-specific Gaussian frontier, transfers its values by empirical moment correction, and extends the same program to pinned calibration curvature \(\rho\).
